title: Finite Gibbs invariance and conditional OS intertwiner boundary
question: What exact invariant finite Gibbs seminorm identity is available, and which additional hypotheses would transfer it into the fixed-beta OS mixture without claiming Hamiltonian thermodynamic identification?
method: Use rho_beta=Z^{-1} exp(-beta H) for a finite self-adjoint H and derive [rho_beta,U_t]=0 by functional calculus.
Apply finite trace cyclicity separately to X^*X and XX^* to prove exact two-sided beta,# isometry.

Check a two-level q=1/2 rational fixture independently and in Lean, then state the OS transfer only as a four-hypothesis conditional implication: seminorm isometry, action intertwining, common-word compatibility and exhaustion control.
finding: The finite Gibbs state is invariant under its own Hamiltonian orbit and its two-sided beta,# seminorm is exactly isometric. An invariant seminorm-isometric Hamiltonian-to-OS intertwiner would transfer this identity to the fixed-beta OS carrier, but the actual Q3 maps, common-word compatibility and exhaustion independence remain unproved.
decision_reason: This is a non-duplicative positive complement to EXP-001064: it replaces the false arbitrary-state shortcut by the exact finite Gibbs condition and names every additional OS identification hypothesis instead of hiding it.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite interface theorem. It does not prove actual Q3 operator history, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, a beta-independent common alpha, a GNS gap, the continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or the TECT production owner.

qft_interface.open: Common finite-to-OS embedding, actual Q3 histories, direct D/delta-D, exhaustion, common alpha, gap and continuum remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: No heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.
